title: Context Window Economics: Semantic Retrieval Pruning vs Raw Chat History

steps.prompt: A customer engagement session reaches 40 turns. If the entire uncompressed raw chat transcript is passed on every new prompt, what operational failure occurs and how is it solved?

options.label: Context saturation increases latency and dilutes model attention; resolve using sliding memory and semantic summaries
options.rationale: Uncompressed history balloons token consumption and degrades LLM reasoning. Implementing sliding-window memory and condensed semantic summaries maintains precision while reducing cost.

options.label: Database heap size limits in Apex are exceeded; resolve by persisting intermediate conversation turns to Big Objects
options.distractorAntipattern: The failure is model token latency and cognitive dilution ("lost in the middle"), not synchronous Apex heap exhaustion.
options.rationale: The primary failure is cognitive dilution and token latency inside the model context window, not an Apex heap limit exception.

options.label: HTTP payload limits on the messaging gateway reject the request; resolve by compressing messages using gzip algorithms
options.distractorAntipattern: Network gateway limits are not breached by chat text; the problem is model context token limits and LLM reasoning accuracy.
options.rationale: Compressing transport payloads does not decrease model token consumption or prevent context saturation inside the LLM attention window.
